public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 85

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

## Counterexample

The conjecture is false for the lexicographic product $C_5[K_4]$. This graph
has minimum even-distance count $9$ and largest induced-tree order $4$. The
conjectured lower bound is therefore $\lceil\sqrt{1 + 2 \cdot 9}\rceil =
\lceil\sqrt{19}\rceil = 5 > 4$.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture85

open SimpleGraph

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 85](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
asked whether every simple connected graph $G$ satisfies
$\operatorname{tree}(G) \geq
\lceil\sqrt{1 + 2\min_v \operatorname{distEven}(v)}\rceil$.
The answer is no, as witnessed by $C_5[K_4]$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
"https://github.com/Kuberwastaken/wowii-63-85-counterexample/blob/cba739842ec59adf7426c180009175b31935701d/lean/WOWII85.lean#L171-L183"]
theorem conjecture85 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
      (G : SimpleGraph α) (_h : G.Connected),
      let minDistEven := (Finset.univ.image (G.distEven ·)).min' (by simp)
      ⌈Real.sqrt (1 + 2 * (minDistEven : ℝ))⌉ ≤
        (G.largestInducedTreeSize : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/-- The largest induced-tree order is a natural number. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ G.largestInducedTreeSize := Nat.zero_le _

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture85

findings.description: The quantified `[Nontrivial α]` restricts the conjecture's right-hand side to graphs with at least two vertices, whereas the source says only “simple connected graph.” This exclusion is not redundant: for the one-vertex graph, `distEven` is 1, `largestInducedTreeSize` is 1, and the proposed lower bound is ⌈√3⌉ = 2. I checked this singleton violation in Lean. Excluding trivial graphs is a plausible intended convention, so this is a modelling question rather than a definite misformalization. The cited nontrivial counterexample and the negative answer remain valid.
findings.source_evidence: DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, all.html, Conjecture 85 (April 4, 2004): “If G is a simple connected graph, then tree(G) ≥ CEIL[sqrt(1 + 2*minimum of dist_even(v))].” Its linked wowIIdefs.js entry 10 defines dist_even(v) as “The number of vertices whose distance from v is an even integer,” and entry 48 defines tree(G) as the number of vertices of a largest induced tree. Neither this entry nor the introductory page explicitly excludes singleton graphs. Read archived copies of http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html and wowIIdefs.js.
findings.suggested_fix: Document and cite the intended exclusion of singleton graphs, and make that restriction explicit in the theorem docstring. If the literal all-connected-graphs formulation is intended instead, replace `[Nontrivial α]` with `[Nonempty α]`; the existing nontrivial counterexample still establishes `answer(False)`.

sources_consulted: https://combinatorialpress.com/cn/archive/ (checked availability of the introductory page's cited 2004 paper; its volume has no article links)
Supplied calibration examples: all eight not_misformalizations cases; past_misformalizations INDEX.md and pr01256, pr01870, pr02295, pr04119, pr04171, pr04282.
review.notes: No other mathematical defects found. The source's formula and invariant definitions match Lean. Connectedness excludes unreachable-distance defaults, and finiteness makes the tree-order supremum bounded and attained; these properties and small boundary cases were checked in /workspace/review/boundaries.lean. The anonymous nonnegativity test is correct. I compiled the cited external proof against the current imported definitions in /workspace/review/external_proof.lean and checked that its theorem establishes the repository's exact statement. Its axioms contain native_decide-generated computation axioms but no sorryAx. Thus the counterexample values 9 and 4, the bound 5, and the solved/False/formal_proof records are supported, notwithstanding the older source table's open marker. The live source was unavailable, so the original list and definition script were read through archived copies.
